# N11. fp4g-patch: the wiring of K15's NVFP4 parameter all-gather into Megatron's parameter sync and TE's weight cast

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Switches: `AK_FP4G_CHECK=first`, `AK_FP4G_POISON=0` (config L34), `AK_FP4G_NOOVERLAP=1` (config L36); armed by K15's `AK_FP4G` · In the submitted runs: **on** (poison off, no-overlap mode on) · Class: **E0** · Rule basis: Graph Execution (TR-8.3)

**L4 v3.** L4 v3 changes this item in one way: with `AK_FP4G_NOOVERLAP=1` every forward parameter gather is finished at its dispatch, so none overlaps compute ("L4 v3: no gather overlap", below). Everything else is L4 v2's. Evidence collected on L4 v2's package (`firmus_gb300_ngpu8_llama8b_l4_nvfp4_v2`, withdrawn from this submission; see [Index](../KERNELS.md)) is labelled so.

## In brief

NVIDIA's recipe all-gathers each bucket group's bf16 weights before the forward (Megatron's distributed optimizer), and
Transformer Engine (TE) then casts each weight to NVFP4 for the GEMMs. N11 (fp4g-patch) is the Python module that puts
[K15](K15_fp4g_param_allgather.md) (fp4g)'s kernels there for the "pure" bucket groups (only NVFP4 GEMM weights and norm
weights): K15's shard cast and all-gather run on a side stream, TE's weight cast is answered from the gathered storage,
and the partial amaxes (maximum absolute values, which set the NVFP4 scales) of the 16×16 tiles that shard boundaries cut join K9's
amax all-reduce. N11 computes no values; the GEMMs read K15's bytes, which equal TE's cast of the full weight: **E0**.
Nothing reads the other ranks' bf16 copies of the gathered weights, which go stale; no code enforces this, and runs with
those copies poisoned to NaN found no reader.

On this image the patch-module kit's L4 v3 version passed, and every scored run's check found 0 differing bytes; the
multi-rank and model-level comparisons ran on L4 v2's image. In L4 v2, one class of run-to-run drift entered at a GEMM
that ran alongside the next group's gather, which N11 dispatches; its cause is unexplained. L4 v3 finishes every forward
parameter gather at its dispatch, and its drift check found no departure ([the index's reproducibility section](../KERNELS.md#run-to-run-reproducibility)).

## What it replaces (Replaces)

- **NVIDIA's code:** stock Megatron-LM `megatron/core/distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py`, class `_ParamAndGradBucketGroup`.
  - `start_param_sync(force_sync)` (L427-582), with the distributed optimizer: one `_coalescing_manager` (PyTorch's
    batching of several collectives into one NCCL group) over the group's `intra_distributed_optimizer_instance_group`,
    and one `all_gather_into_tensor` per bucket, from this rank's shard into the bucket's flat bf16 buffer `param_data`
    (L549-572). It is asynchronous when `overlap_param_gather` is set and the sync is not forced (L450), the manager then
    kept as the group's `param_gather_handle` (L573-579). A forced sync with a gather outstanding waits for it, runs
    `_post_param_sync` and returns (L441-446). The method sets `param_gather_dispatched` (L582).
  - `finish_param_sync` (L584-644) dispatches the group's gather if it has not been dispatched (L603-604). With a handle
    outstanding, it waits on it, clears it, dispatches the next group's `start_param_sync` (L606-619) and runs
    `_post_param_sync` (L644). DDP's forward pre-hook (`distributed_data_parallel.py` L534-557) calls it for the bucket
    group of every parameter of a module, before the module runs.
  - `_post_param_sync` (L345-387) acts only when `reuse_grad_buf_for_mxfp8_param_ag` is set, or on parameters held in
    TE's quantized storage (FP8 or NVFP4 parameter tensors, L81-89).
  - TE then casts each gathered weight with the recipe's 2D NVFP4 weight quantizer (K15, Replaces).
- **The stock line numbers** were read on dev image 0929's copy of Megatron-LM (the image's is `f6c33bde`). N7 (X7)'s
  patches `firmus/patches/mcore/0003-x7-ddp.patch` and `0004-x7-param-and-grad-buffer.patch`, applied to those copies,
  give the image's installed files byte for byte (`/FIRMUS_STACK_SHA256.txt` L5-6); `0004` changes nothing before L652.
- **In L4 without K15**, every group takes this path, and N6 (nvfp4p) routes the weight casts to K9's weight amax and
  K10's weight cast, both byte-identical to TE's ([N6](N06_nvfp4p_patch.md), [K9](K09_nvfp4w_weight_amax.md),
  [K10](K10_w2d7_weight_cast.md)); after each optimizer step K9 computes every weight's amax on this rank's shards and
  MAX-all-reduces the buffer.
- **The submitted runs' DDP settings:** `overlap_param_gather=True`, `use_distributed_optimizer=True`,
  `num_distributed_optimizer_instances=1` and `reuse_grad_buf_for_mxfp8_param_ag=False` (`result_1.txt` L402);
  `fp8_param=False` and `fp4_param=False` (L673, L692): the parameters are plain bf16 tensors. The same in all ten logs.
- **What N11 replaces**, for each pure group (only NVFP4 GEMM weights and 1-D bf16 norm weights; K15, Gate):
  1. **The gather.** The wrapped `start_param_sync` runs K15's dispatch instead of the bf16 all-gather: on a side stream,
     `shard_quant2` casts this rank's shard into the group's FP4 and tile-scale images, the norm values are packed into a
     norm image, and one coalesced asynchronous all-gather moves the three images. N11's handle takes Megatron's place.
  2. **The wait.** When `finish_param_sync` waits on that handle, N11's `_Handle.wait` runs `post_ag3` (the column-wise
     data and both GEMM-swizzled scale tensors) and copies the norm values back into the bf16 buffer.
  3. **TE's weight cast.** N6's `tex.quantize` wrapper asks N11 first; for a gathered weight, N11 returns the gathered
     NVFP4 storage instead of a new cast.
  4. **K9's amax all-reduce.** Before it, N11 zeroes the slot region that setup appended to K9's weight-amax buffer and
     runs `split_amax2`, which writes this rank's partial amaxes of the cut tile-rows into the slots.
  - Besides these, a one-time setup lays out the images and the cut tile-rows, and an in-run check runs (Enablement).
- **Not changed.** Groups that are not pure run Megatron's own `start_param_sync`: in the submitted runs group 0, which holds the output layer, and group 8, which holds the embedding (`result_1.txt` L916); L4 v3's no-overlap mode adds a wait after group 0's. N11 does not change `finish_param_sync`, DDP's pre-hook, the gradient buffer, the reduce-scatter or the bucket layout.

## Why the result is the same (Equivalence)

**Class E0:** the GEMMs read bit-identical bytes. N11 changes where and when the gather runs and who answers TE's cast;
the bytes are K15's. For one pure group g, each step:

```
NVIDIA:
  optimizer step:  each rank writes its shard of g's bf16 param_data
  forward, before g's first module (DDP pre-hook -> finish_param_sync(g)):
                   wait for g's bf16 all-gather (dispatched earlier, asynchronous); dispatch the next group's
  each GEMM:       W_q = TE_2D_cast(W_bf16)     (amax over the full weight, then the cast)
N11:
  optimizer step:  K9's amax update: before_allreduce (zero the slots; split_amax2), then the MAX all-reduce
  start_param_sync(g) -> _dispatch(g): side stream waits for the current stream; on the side stream: shard_quant2,
                   pack the norms, one coalesced all-gather of the 3 images; the handle goes into g.param_gather_handle
  finish_param_sync(g) -> handle.wait() -> _Handle.wait: on the side stream: wait for the all-gather, post_ag3,
                   copy the norms back; then the current stream waits for the side stream
  each GEMM:       tex.quantize(W) -> N6 -> weight_quantize -> the gathered NVFP4 storage
```
In L4 v3, `_Handle.wait` runs right after `_dispatch(g)`, and `finish_param_sync(g)` gets a handle with nothing left to
wait for ("L4 v3: no gather overlap").

**The argument** (lines of `ak_l8b_fp4g_patch.py` unless named).
1. **The bytes.** Given the shards the optimizer step wrote and the amaxes K9's all-reduce completed, every byte K15
   writes equals TE's 2D cast of the full bf16 weight (K15, Equivalence: the amaxes are completed before the cast, one
   rank writes each tile's scale with the tile's full amax, and the cast works element by element). N11 adds no
   arithmetic.
2. **The inputs are the right ones.** The partial amaxes of the cut tile-rows are written just before K9's MAX all-reduce (L537-546; `ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L450-453), so they enter the same maximum. The dispatch's side stream first waits for the current stream (L190), so the shard cast reads the shards and amaxes written before it.
3. **The storage is ready before it is read.** N11's handle sits where Megatron keeps its own (L233-243, with the no-overlap wait at L234-237), so `finish_param_sync`, called by DDP's pre-hook of the group's first module, waits on it where stock waits for the bf16 gather. `_Handle.wait` ends with the current stream waiting for the side stream (L171-183), so every kernel issued afterwards on the current stream sees the finished images; the GEMMs read them through the cast answer.
4. **The other branches follow stock** (L226-240). Without overlap, or on a forced sync, N11 dispatches and waits at once, as stock's synchronous gather does; a forced sync with a gather outstanding waits for it and returns, as stock does. Stock's `_post_param_sync` is not called on these two paths (it has nothing to do for a pure group; Assumptions).
5. **The cast answer is narrow** (L144-161, L123-141). It answers only for a tensor whose data pointer and size are a registered gathered weight, and only for TE's `NVFP4Quantizer` with 2D quantization. An in-place update of a module workspace (the cached NVFP4 copy of the weight that TE's QKV and projection modules rewrite every step) must target the gathered storage, which is already written; N11 returns it unchanged (counted as a skipped workspace update), and any other workspace raises. A call without an output gets a new NVFP4 tensor object over the same gathered buffers, carrying the caller's quantizer and only the usages it asks for (counted as a wrapper). Every other call goes on to N6's own path.
6. **Mixed groups are stock** (L216-225; in L4 v3 group 0's gather is also waited for at its dispatch, L218-224), and the gradient side is untouched. **The stale bf16 copies** are a precondition, not part of the argument (Assumptions).

The in-run check (Enablement) compares every gathered byte with TE's cast of the re-gathered bf16 weight.

**State kept between calls:** `_STATE` (each pure group's plan with its images, views and kernel tables, the lookup of
gathered weights by data pointer and size, the side stream, and the counters `checks`, `gathers`, `noop_calls`,
`wrap_calls`) and the plan on each pure bucket group as `_ak_fp4g`, built once at setup; between a dispatch and its wait,
the handle in the group's `param_gather_handle` (L75-77, L200, L241-243, L311-313, L490, L554-557). The no-overlap mode
adds `patched` and the wait counters `nooverlap_fp4g` and `nooverlap_g0` (L77, L224, L237, L633), and a group's handle is
`_NOOP_HANDLE` between the dispatch and `finish_param_sync`.

## Numerics (Numerics)

None of its own. N11 computes no floating-point value: it moves the bytes K15 writes and copies the bf16 norm values
unchanged. The numerics are K15's, which are TE's (K15, Numerics). The poison mode writes the NaN pattern `0x7FC0` into
the stale bf16 copies; it is off in the submitted runs (Enablement).

## Optimizer and gradient clipping (Optimizer, Gradient clipping)

- Optimizer: not applicable. N11 runs inside the optimizer step (setup, the slots before K9's all-reduce, the check) but
  reads and writes no optimizer state, gradient or learning rate.
- Gradient clipping: not applicable. N11 does not touch the gradients or the gradient norm.

## Inputs it accepts (Shape specialisation)

### Gate

- **Which groups:** K15's gate (K15, Gate). A group is pure when every bucket has a bf16 buffer whose size is a multiple of 256 × DP, holds at least one selected NVFP4 weight, and holds nothing else but such weights (each with its offset and both dimensions multiples of 256) and 1-D bf16 tensors (`ak_l8b_fp4g_patch.py` L326-359). In the submitted runs: 109 of 128 weights in 7 of 9 groups (`result_1.txt` L916).
- **Which calls:** the wrapper acts only on a bucket group that carries N11's plan while N11 is active (L216-217), and any other group runs Megatron's own method; the cast answer acts only on a registered gathered weight with a 2D `NVFP4Quantizer` (L146-152), and everything else goes to N6.
- **What raises:** an armed N11 without K9's weight-amax update (at import, L56-61); the no-overlap switch with a value
  other than 0 or 1, or without `AK_FP4G` (at import, L66-72); more than one model chunk (L314-316); no pure group
  (L497-499); with the no-overlap switch, a wrapper not installed or a stock-group count other than one (L523-530), and a
  `param_and_grad_buffer` without `_ParamAndGradBucketGroup` (at import, L624-626); a second distributed optimizer (in
  N6, `ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L424-425); a workspace update that does not target the gathered storage (L153-157). The
  import hook does not wrap a method it has already wrapped (L628-629).

### Assumptions not checked in code

K15 lists the preconditions of the gathered bytes (K15, "Assumptions not checked in code"); those N11's wiring carries
are summarised here, with the ones only N11 has.

- **No reader of the stale bf16 copies** (K15's). Outside this rank's shard, the bf16 buffer of a pure group is never
  gathered again, and no code stops a reader. What keeps it true: every GEMM gets the gathered storage through the cast
  answer; K10's and K9's checks skip these weights (`ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L338-340, L460-468); runs with the stale
  copies poisoned found no reader (Evidence); the submitted runs ran with poison off. If it failed: **silent wrong result.**
- **Every consumer runs after the group's wait** (K15's): Megatron calls the stored handle's `wait` through `finish_param_sync` before the group's first module runs. What keeps it true: DDP's pre-hook does this for its own gather, unchanged; in the captured training graph an ordering probe found every producer ordered before every group-first consumer, and no consumer starting before its producer finished, over 1,152 steps × 7 boundaries × 4 ranks (record R10), on L4 v2's image; in L4 v3 the wait runs at the dispatch. If it failed: **silent wrong result.**
- **Stock's `_post_param_sync` has nothing to do for a pure group.** On a forced sync and on the synchronous path, N11's wrapper does not call it, and it drops stock's `param_sync_via_bucket_group` assertion (L226-240, against stock L439-446, L580-581). What keeps it true: a pure group holds only plain bf16 parameters (L335-350), and `reuse_grad_buf_for_mxfp8_param_ag=False` (`result_1.txt` L402); on the overlapped path stock's `finish_param_sync` still calls it after N11's wait. The no-overlap mode clears bucket group 0's handle at the dispatch, so `finish_param_sync` also skips that group's `_post_param_sync` (stock L606-644); group 0's parameters are plain bf16 tensors too. If it failed (a configuration that needed it): the step would be skipped, a **silent** difference. No code checks it.
- **K9's all-reduce and each pure group's gather span the same ranks** (K15's): one distributed-optimizer instance
  (`num_distributed_optimizer_instances=1`, `result_1.txt` L402). If it failed: **raise** at the check.
- **The weights' addresses and storage do not change after setup** (K15's). If it failed: **silent wrong result** or a
  memory fault; a replaced module workspace raises.
- **No one holds K9's weight-amax buffer when setup replaces it** with a longer one that adds the slot region (L379-385); no code checks that nothing cached the old one. What keeps it true: setup runs once (L311-313), in K9's first update, right after K9 builds its table (`ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L418-423); K6 (X9)'s fused optimizer epilogue takes the buffer only once that table exists, and caches it from then on (`firmus/patches/mcore/0001-x9-distrib-optimizer.patch` L283-296). If it failed: the epilogue would write the amaxes into a buffer N6 no longer reads; K9's one-time check of the epilogue's amaxes compares the buffer N6 reads with a fresh pass over the shards (`ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L430-447), so this would most likely **raise**; not tested.
- **The order of the two `start_param_sync` wrappers does not matter here.** N5 (X9 wiring)'s early all-gather wraps N11's wrapper (module docstring L40-41; `firmus/patches/mcore/0001-x9-distrib-optimizer.patch` L53-75). Its early group is group 8 (`result_1.txt` L918), which is not pure, so N11 passes it to Megatron's own code. If it failed (a layout whose early group is pure): not analysed; the submitted layout cannot reach it.
- **L4 v3: the no-overlap mode waits for exactly the gathers the forward overlapped:** every pure group's gather and the
  one stock group with no next gather (bucket group 0). For group 8, the embedding's, it relies on N5's early all-gather,
  which gathers and waits for it inside the optimizer step, before the forward starts ([N5](N05_x9_wiring.md); its ARMED
  line is `result_1.txt` L918). What keeps it true: setup raises unless exactly one
  stock group has no next gather (L523-530), and the gate's `fp4g no-overlap` row requires both waits to have fired in the
  warm-up (`firmus_ak/run_start_gate.py` L58-62). If it failed (a stock group other than 0 overlapping a GEMM): not a
  wrong result; that gather would overlap compute as in L4 v2.

### Benchmark detection

N11 tests no shape constant, layer count or model size. Its tests are K15's (Megatron's parameter-name suffixes, dtype,
layout, the quantizer's type and settings, divisibility by 256): they identify the code being replaced, a property of the
software stack, not of the benchmark (Benchmark detection, TR-2.3). The development version's program-name test was
removed (Source).

## How it is switched on and checked at run time (Enablement)

- **Arming:** K15's `AK_FP4G` (read at L55) arms N11. The import-time refusal, the import hook and the kernel directory are in K15's Enablement.
- **`AK_FP4G_CHECK=first`** (config L34; read at L62, default `"first"`): `first` checks once, at the first optimizer step after setup; `off` never checks; any other value (the patch-module kit used `all`) checks at every optimizer step (L555-556).
- **`AK_FP4G_POISON=0`** (config L34; read at L63, default `"0"`): with `1`, setup fills the other ranks' shards of every pure bucket's bf16 buffer with the NaN pattern `0x7FC0` (L501-512), so that a read of the stale copies returns NaN; the docstring calls it a mode for proof runs only (L28-30). The submitted switches reach neither this mode nor the `all` and `off` check modes ([Code present but not executed](../KERNELS.md#code-present-but-not-executed-with-the-submitted-switches)).
- **`AK_FP4G_NOOVERLAP=1`** (config L36; read at L66-69,
  default `"0"`): the no-overlap mode ("L4 v3: no gather overlap" below). Any value other than `0` or `1` raises at
  import, and so does `1` without `AK_FP4G=1` (L67-72).
- **Setup:** once, at the end of the first optimizer step, in K9's weight-amax update (`ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L418-423, called from L1706). It raises as listed under Gate and prints the ARMED line; with the no-overlap switch it then checks that the mode can install and prints the mode's ARMED line (L523-534).
- **The check** (L550-613):
  - it synchronises the device and re-gathers every pure bucket's bf16 shards with a plain `all_gather_into_tensor` into a scratch buffer (L558-567);
  - it casts each weight with TE's original `tex.quantize` and the weight's quantizer, and compares six buffers byte by byte (row-wise and column-wise data and scales, both amaxes) and the swizzle flag (L568-592), and every norm with its re-gathered values (L593-598);
  - it all-reduces the count over the group, prints, and raises on any difference, on every rank (L600-613). Only rank 0's line reaches the log; the count it prints is over all ranks.
  - It runs at the start of the optimizer step, before the step writes (`ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L1697-1699). N11 is not active at the first optimizer step, so with `first` the one check is at the second optimizer step, in NVIDIA's warm-up; no scored step is checked. The line's "optimizer step 1" counts from 0 (L608); the leaf's comment above the switches (config L33) says "checked at the first optimizer step", the first after setup.
- **Run-start gate:** its row `fp4g` passes when N11 is active and at least one check ran, or the check is off (`firmus_ak/run_start_gate.py` L53-57). Its row `fp4g no-overlap` passes only when both waits fired during the warm-up: at least one FP4G gather finished at its dispatch and one bucket-group-0 gather waited for at its dispatch (L58-62). The gate's verdict is per rank ([Enablement and fail-loud behaviour](../KERNELS.md#enablement-and-fail-loud-behaviour)); N11's check all-reduces its count, so every rank reaches the same check verdict.

## L4 v3: no gather overlap (`AK_FP4G_NOOVERLAP`)

L4 v3 is L4 v2 with one change, made here: with `AK_FP4G_NOOVERLAP=1` (config
L36), no parameter gather of the forward overlaps compute. Its switch, raises, gate row and
ARMED line (L531-534) are under Enablement, Gate and Evidence; `firmus/ak/pkg/CHANGES_vs_validated.md` L53-63 lists the 8 edits.
- **What moves: two waits.** After `_dispatch` of a pure group, the handle's `wait()` runs at once: the side stream waits
  for the coalesced all-gather, `post_ag3` writes the gathered storage, the norms are unpacked, and the current stream
  joins the side stream (`ak_l8b_fp4g_patch.py` L234-237); `finish_param_sync` then gets `_NOOP_HANDLE`, whose `wait()`
  does nothing, and still dispatches the next group (L204-211). After Megatron's own `start_param_sync` of the one stock
  group with no next gather (bucket group 0: the output layer, the final norm and the last layers' weights), the current
  stream waits for its all-gather at once and the handle is cleared (L218-225; Assumptions). The same kernels run on the
  same buffers in the same order; only when the current stream waits changes, so no value changes. A forced sync
  (evaluation) and N5's early all-gather of group 8 are unchanged.
- **Why.** In L4 v2 the next group's dispatch (`shard_quant2`, the norm pack, the coalesced NCCL all-gather) ran on the
  side stream beside the fc1 GEMM of the group-first consumer layer, and under that overlap one rank's fc1 output
  occasionally differed from identical inputs. The probes' `nooverlap` wrapper, which these lines implement inside the
  module, removed it in 7 of 7 loops ([the index's reproducibility section](../KERNELS.md#run-to-run-reproducibility)).
- **Cost.** On the submitted trays and layout, 0.27508 s per step against L4 v2's 0.27085 s (+1.56 %); over the ten
  scored runs, the time per evaluation interval is 0.83 % above L4 v2's ten (on other trays).

## Approval (Approval)

None needed: N11 is E0. It changes where and when the parameter gather runs and who answers TE's weight cast; the bytes
the GEMMs read are bit-identical to TE's cast of the full weight (K15). Rule basis: Graph Execution (TR-8.3), which
allows mathematically equivalent changes to the non-weight parts of the computation graph.

## Evidence (Evidence)

**Result on the submitted image:** PASS: the patch-module kit's L4 v3 version found the gathered weights byte-identical to
TE's 2D cast in 9 of 9 checks per run, with the no-overlap mode on and off, and losses and evaluations bit-identical to
the gather-off control; every scored run's check found 0 bytes differ.
